2
Osmium, a naturally occurring element, has a density of 23 000 kg m–3.
What is also a value of the density of osmium?
A
2.3 × 104
µg cm–3
B
2.3 × 104
g cm–3
C
2.3 kg cm–3
D
2.3 × 10–2
kg cm–3

hints: Notice the given density is $23000 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ but the options with $\text{kg cm}^{-3}$ use cubic centimetres, so focus on how $\text{m}^3$ converts to $\text{cm}^3$.
Recall that $1 \text{ m} = 100 \text{ cm}$, so cubing gives $1 \text{ m}^3 = 100^3 \text{ cm}^3 = 10^6 \text{ cm}^3$.
Divide the mass by the larger number of volume units: $23000$ divided by $10^6$, and write the result in standard form with units $\text{kg cm}^{-3}$ to compare with options C and D.
walkthrough: Write the given density as a fraction: $23000 \text{ kg}$ per $1 \text{ m}^3$.
Convert the volume unit using $1 \text{ m} = 100 \text{ cm}$, so $1 \text{ m}^3 = (100 \text{ cm})^3 = 1 \times 10^6 \text{ cm}^3$.
Substitute this volume: density $= 23000 \text{ kg} / 10^6 \text{ cm}^3$.
Calculate the number: $23000 / 10^6 = 0.023 = 2.3 \times 10^{-2}$, with units $\text{kg cm}^{-3}$.
Check that $2.3 \text{ kg cm}^{-3}$ would be 100 times larger, and the $\text{g cm}^{-3}$ and $\mu\text{g cm}^{-3}$ options do not match after prefix conversion. This is option D.

A.explanation: This is far too small. $2.3 \times 10^4 \text{ } \mu\text{g cm}^{-3}$ equals only $2.3 \times 10^{-2} \text{ g cm}^{-3}$, while osmium is about $23 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$.

B.explanation: This is 1000 times too large. $2.3 \times 10^4 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$ would equal $2.3 \times 10^7 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$, not $2.3 \times 10^4 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$.

C.explanation: This is 100 times too large. $2.3 \text{ kg cm}^{-3}$ would equal $2.3 \times 10^6 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ because $1 \text{ m}^3 = 10^6 \text{ cm}^3$.

D.explanation: This is correct. Dividing $23000 \text{ kg}$ by $10^6 \text{ cm}^3$ gives $0.023 \text{ kg cm}^{-3} = 2.3 \times 10^{-2} \text{ kg cm}^{-3}$.
